answer: Tie every voting seat to a distinct live data feed the agent must serve as an oracle. Each agent picks an independent source, say a tide gauge at one coastal inlet or a flow meter on a river delta, and publishes signed hourly readings that peers spot-check against the public record. Clones cannot just mirror one feed: readings that track another seat too closely get flagged, and both seats lose their votes. Licensing or installing a unique source costs about $40 a month, so 500 fake seats would cost an attacker $20,000 monthly.
